packet-09 - unverified image reading (blind; no identification seen in context)

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001.jpg, reduced overview)
- One photograph of many fragments on black ground, colour checker lower left, cm scale at right (~38 cm). All pieces upright as photographed.
- Two tiny scraps upper left (a thin strip and a small square) carrying modern pencil notes; no text read from overview.
- Top row, three strips (each roughly 8-9 cm wide, ~13-15 cm tall): left strip damaged at left edge with brown stains near top; has a red rubric/display word in a larger Gothic textualis about 2/3 down (overview shows something like "[...]mona" upside-down? and below "[...]ndus" in red); middle strip plain text with a red mark at left; right strip with ragged left edge, a red stroke near top right, text in narrow column.
- Bottom row, four pieces (~8-9 cm wide, ~13 cm tall): the second piece has a red display word at top right; the third has a red display word near bottom left ("[...]nus"? with a red paraph). Several pieces show worm-hole/insect damage (black holes) and vertical folds.
- Script: small, dense Gothic cursive/notula-type hand, many lines per piece (overview suggests ~30-40 lines per strip); appears single-column on each strip, with ruling visible as fine vertical lines. Modern pencil shelfmark-type notes ("STA ... Fg ...") on several pieces.
- Interpretation (tentative): strips cut from one or more paper or parchment leaves of a densely written text with occasional red display headings; the red display words on the top-left and bottom-middle pieces appear to be written in larger textualis, possibly inverted relative to the main text on one strip - to be checked in tiles.
